column2: Revision_Deflation_CJT_and_Kohn-Sham_definition_C: checks of the pairing with contact self-interaction and exchange of the Vorton-Scalar (pc-..)

column4: pairing amplitudes of the four independent contact channels in the hidden-axis channel, for two particles of mass M with momenta p, -p in ordinary space that scatter into p', -p' (E = sqrt(M^2 + p^2), E' likewise): F_0 = (E E' + M^2 - p.p')/(2 E E'), F_1 = (3 E E' - 2 M^2 - p.p')/(E E'), F_7 = (3 E E' + 2 M^2 - p.p')/(E E'), F_8 = -(E E' - M^2 - p.p')/(2 E E'). Direct evaluation with the 256 matrices M_K and the projectors on the states of positive energy agrees with these closed forms for 40 random sets of mass and momenta on each of the two spacetimes (7+1; 4+4 in the quantized-sector form): largest deviation 1.8e-15; the two spacetimes give the same amplitudes (largest difference 7.1e-15). The pairing potential of the contact interaction is V = g_0eff F_0 + g_1eff F_1 + g_7eff F_7 + g_8eff F_8

the reduction to four invariants and the pairing amplitudes. For two particles at rest the nine amplitudes are the exact pair couplings of the hidden-axis pair, q = (1, 1, -9, -9, -5, -5, 5, 5, 0) (largest deviation 0.0e0). At general momenta the relations (1 + F) I = 0 hold for the part of the amplitudes that is even in the angle between p and p' (the sum of the direct and of the exchange scattering of two identical particles): the amplitudes of the ranks 2 to 6, evaluated directly, equal the prescribed combinations of F_0, F_1, F_7, F_8 (largest deviation 1.2e-14); the parts odd in the angle do not (deviation up to 13.79), and they do not contribute to a contact interaction in a pair state of zero orbital angular momentum. Consequence for the model: with a strictly local interaction four couplings suffice; when the contact interaction is given a range, the model is DEFINED by giving this range to the four channels S, V, A, P. The closed forms are derived for momenta in ordinary space; if the momentum has a component along the hidden axis x0 itself they do not hold (deviation up to 0.92), because the pair operator points along that axis

the two forms of the 4+4 model in the two kinds of vector pairs along the extra axes (momenta in ordinary space). The pair along the hidden axis, psi^T Cm.gamma^0 psi, consists of one particle of each half W = +-1 of the field; the pairs along the deflating coordinates, psi^T Cm.gamma^t psi (t = 5, 6, 7), consist of two particles of the same half. Direct evaluation with the 256 matrices of each form and the projectors on the states of positive energy, 20 random sets of mass and momenta in each of nine cases: in the quantized-sector form the amplitudes of all four pairs are the closed forms F_0, F_1, F_7, F_8 of check pc-P1 (so are those of the pairs along x5 on 7+1); in the COVARIANT form the amplitudes of the pairs along x5, x6, x7 are the same closed forms, and those of the hidden-axis pair are MINUS the closed forms (largest deviation over all cases 2.2e-15; for all nine ranks the part even in the angle is the prescribed combination of the four, with the same sign: 1.2e-14). At rest the nine amplitudes of the covariant form in the hidden-axis channel are the exact pair couplings of check 44c-S9, (-1, -1, 9, 9, 5, 5, -5, -5, 0) (largest deviation 0.0e0). The pairing potential of the contact interaction is therefore V = s (g_0eff F_0 + g_1eff F_1 + g_7eff F_7 + g_8eff F_8) with s = +1, except for the hidden-axis pair in the covariant form, where s = -1

the exchange of the Vorton-Scalar is a self-interaction of finite range: (i) without contact couplings the pairing kernel of this program equals the kernel of the main project (four sets of parameters, five pairs of momenta each: largest relative difference 1.1e-15); (ii) the scalar contact coupling g_0eff = -g_VS^2/m_s^2 with the range parameter m_ct = m_s (the mass of the heavy boson whose exchange the contact coupling stands for) gives exactly the kernel of the exchange of the radial mode (largest relative difference 3.3e-16): g_0eff(q) = -g_VS^2/(q^2 + m_s^2), and likewise g_8eff(q) = +g_VS^2/(q^2 + m_ph^2) for the phase mode

the gap along the deflation clock with contact couplings that act with the sign of the closed forms (7+1: the hidden-axis pair; 4+4, quantized-sector form: all four vector pairs along the extra axes; 4+4, covariant form: the pairs along x5, x6, x7), 72 clock readings in four sets of (m_s, k_F), seven variants each: without contact couplings the gaps of the earlier calculation (exchange of the two modes of the Vorton-Scalar) are reproduced (largest relative difference 6.6e-16); a scalar contact attraction raises the gap, a vector contact repulsion and a mass of the phase mode lower it (verified at every clock reading with a gap above 1e-6 E_F); for small gaps T_c/gap is within 0.001 of the weak-coupling value 0.567. Example: for m_s = m, k_F = 0.5 m at tau_d = 2.04 (g_VS = 2.771): gap/E_F = 0.0246 (exchange alone), 0.2968 (with scalar contact), 0.1961 (author's ratio), 0.0006 (with vector repulsion 0.3), 0.1287 (with axial coupling), 0.0006 (contact alone), 0.0197 (phase mode of mass 0.3 m)

the gap of the HIDDEN-AXIS pair in the COVARIANT form of the 4+4 model, where the contact couplings enter the pairing potential with the opposite sign (check pc-P5), for the same variants and clock readings: a scalar contact attraction (g_0eff < 0) now LOWERS the gap, with or without the vector repulsion of the author's ratio, an axial coupling g_7eff < 0 lowers it, and a vector contact repulsion (g_1eff > 0) RAISES it (verified at every clock reading at which the gap of the exchange alone exceeds 1e-6 E_F); the contact couplings of the author's signs alone (variant 5) give no gap in this channel at any of the 72 clock readings (72 without gap). Consequence: in the covariant form the self-interaction removes the degeneracy of the four vector pairs along the extra axes and selects the direction of the order parameter. With the exchange of the Vorton-Scalar and the contact couplings of the variants 1 to 4: variant 1: the pairs along x5, x6, x7 have the larger gap at 53 readings, the hidden-axis pair at 0; variant 2: the pairs along x5, x6, x7 have the larger gap at 53 readings, the hidden-axis pair at 0; variant 3: the pairs along x5, x6, x7 have the larger gap at 0 readings, the hidden-axis pair at 51; variant 4: the pairs along x5, x6, x7 have the larger gap at 51 readings, the hidden-axis pair at 0. Example: for m_s = m, k_F = 0.5 m at tau_d = 2.04 (g_VS = 2.771): gap/E_F of the hidden-axis pair in the covariant form = 0.0246 (exchange alone), 0.0000 (with scalar contact), 0.0000 (author's ratio), 0.2246 (with vector repulsion 0.3), 0.0007 (with axial coupling), 0.0000 (contact alone)
